opening: can you help with our churn?

facts.situation: we run a subscription internet service and every month some people just leave, we only notice after they are gone
facts.goal: i want to know which of our current customers are likely to leave next month, before it happens
facts.data: the file i just sent, one row per customer with plan, spend, tickets and if they churned the month after
facts.decision: our retention team will call the risky ones and offer them a discount
facts.other: the team can only call maybe a few hundred people a month so we need the list ranked

opening: people keep cancelling on us, its frustrating

facts.situation: we're a small hotel booking agency, lots of bookings get cancelled last minute and rooms stay empty
facts.goal: when a new booking comes in i'd like to know right away how likely it is to be cancelled
facts.data: our bookings export, with lead time, price, channel, free cancellation and whether it was cancelled in the end
facts.decision: we would overbook a bit on the risky ones or ask for a deposit
facts.other: free cancellation bookings are the worst for us i think

opening: I need some kind of weekly report on our subscribers

facts.situation: I manage customer success at a software company, my director wants something every week about subscribers
facts.goal: honestly what she wants is a list every monday of the customers who are going to cancel in the coming month, so we reach them before they go
facts.data: we have a customer table with plan, tenure, monthly spend, support tickets and a flag if they left the next month, history of about two years
facts.decision: each account manager gets the names of their at-risk customers and calls them that week
facts.other: we already have charts of past churn, that part isn't the problem, it's knowing who is next

opening: our returns are killing us

facts.situation: online shop selling home stuff, a lot of orders come back as returned and it costs us shipping twice
facts.goal: when an order is placed i want to flag the ones that will probably be returned
facts.data: the sales file, the status column says if an order was returned or completed
facts.decision: flagged orders get a quick call or extra product info before we ship them
facts.other: we only know the status some weeks after delivery

opening: how can I analyze my customer

facts.situation: we're a telecom reseller and marketing treats everybody the same, i think there are different kinds of customers hiding in there
facts.goal: find natural groups of customers we didn't define ourselves, like personas, based on how they use and pay
facts.data: customer table I uploaded, the segment column is old and nobody trusts it
facts.decision: marketing will build a different campaign for each group
facts.other: i don't want just the old segments again, i want the data to tell us the groups

opening: I have lots of travel data and dont know what to do with it

facts.situation: travel agency, we sell trips to many destinations and our offers feel random
facts.goal: discover what types of travellers we have, groups we can give a name to, like last minute budget people or early planners
facts.data: a few years of bookings: destination, nationality, how early they book, price, channel, if they cancelled
facts.decision: we'll design packages and newsletters for each type
facts.other: we never did any segmenting before, all ideas are welcome

opening: I have data analysis problems

facts.situation: i'm new as analyst here and my manager wants basic facts about our customers for a meeting
facts.goal: average monthly spend per plan and per city, and how many churned in each segment
facts.data: the customers file i sent
facts.decision: it goes into a slide for the quarterly meeting, thats it
facts.other: just numbers about what is there now, nothing fancy

opening: my boss asked me something about last year and I'm lost

facts.situation: we sell sports gear in shops and online, my boss wants to know where our money came from last year
facts.goal: which region and which channel brought the most revenue last year, and the totals
facts.data: an orders table with date, region, channel, category, amount and status
facts.decision: he'll use it to plan where to open next store
facts.other: cancelled orders should not count i guess

opening: I want to build a model of our sales

facts.situation: board meeting next week and they asked me to show how our sales look
facts.goal: by model i mean a breakdown, how last year's sales split by product category and channel and how each month went
facts.data: this sales export, all orders of last year
facts.decision: i put it in the board deck to explain what happened
facts.other: no forecasting needed, they only care about what already happened

opening: can you take a look at our booking stuff

facts.situation: we work with tour operators and they keep asking us questions about our guests
facts.goal: for each nationality, what share booked with free cancellation, and the average lead time per destination
facts.data: bookings file attached
facts.decision: we send these figures to our partners
facts.other: only bookings of this year please if possible

opening: how are our support tickets doing?

facts.situation: I lead the support team for a subscription app, there is a feeling premium users complain more
facts.goal: compare how many tickets premium vs basic customers opened in the last three months, and per city
facts.data: customer table that has plan, city and a count of support tickets in the last 90 days
facts.decision: if premium really complain more i will ask for one more agent for them
facts.other: i just need the facts, not a prediction

opening: need help with our customers list

facts.situation: our call team wants to contact unhappy premium customers in Berlin this week
facts.goal: give me the actual customers, row by row, the ones in Berlin on premium plan with more than 3 tickets lately
facts.data: customer file uploaded
facts.decision: i download it as excel and hand it to the call team
facts.other: i dont need averages or charts, i need the names and ids

opening: our data is all over the place

facts.situation: we have two webshops and each exports orders in its own way, dates look different, some orders appear twice
facts.goal: one clean table of all orders from both shops, same date format, no duplicates
facts.data: two csv exports of orders, the columns are almost the same but named differently
facts.decision: our accountant will use the clean table every month
facts.other: one shop writes amounts with comma as decimal, the other with dot

opening: the export from our system is kinda ugly

facts.situation: we're moving to a new CRM and it wants customers, not orders
facts.goal: turn this into one row per customer with total spend, number of orders, first and last order date
facts.data: the sales export i uploaded, one row per order
facts.decision: i import the result into the CRM
facts.other: returned orders shouldnt be counted in the spend

opening: I got two files that should talk to each other

facts.situation: travel company, bookings live in one system and customer details in another
facts.goal: put them together, one row per booking with the customer info next to it
facts.data: a bookings export with customer_id and a customer file with the same id, signup date, city and so on
facts.decision: our freelance analyst wants a single file to start working
facts.other: some bookings have no matching customer, keep them anyway

opening: my manager keeps asking the same numbers every monday

facts.situation: every week i copy sales into excel by hand and send it around, it takes me half a morning
facts.goal: a page that keeps itself updated with weekly sales by region and channel so people just look at it
facts.data: the sales table, it gets new orders every day
facts.decision: i send the link once and stop doing the excel every monday
facts.other: the sales team should be able to filter by region themselves

opening: is there a way to keep an eye on bookings?

facts.situation: operations team of a tour company, we only see problems when its too late
facts.goal: a screen in the office that shows bookings and cancellations per destination, refreshed every day
facts.data: our booking system, with dates, destination, channel, price and cancellations
facts.decision: the team checks it every morning and reacts if a destination looks bad
facts.other: nothing complicated, just always up to date

opening: we need to track our subscriber base better

facts.situation: leadership asks every month how many subscribers we have, the churn and the spend, and its always a scramble
facts.goal: one place with active subscribers, churn rate and spend per plan that updates each month on its own
facts.data: a customer table with plan, segment, monthly spend and churn, refreshed monthly
facts.decision: leadership opens it before the monthly review
facts.other: they want to see the trend month after month, not one snapshot

opening: my sales are weird lately

facts.situation: last month our revenue went down a lot compared to the month before and nobody knows why
facts.goal: understand what caused the drop, which region or channel or category, and what we should do about it
facts.data: sales file with all orders of this year
facts.decision: i need to tell the owner next week what we change
facts.other: we changed our delivery partner around that time, maybe that matters

opening: something is off with our summer season

facts.situation: this summer way more bookings got cancelled than last summer
facts.goal: find out why cancellations jumped compared to last year and what to change

facts.decision: we may change our free cancellation policy or the channels we sell on
facts.other: we started selling on a new booking website this spring

opening: online isnt doing good for us

facts.situation: our online orders fell this quarter compared to last quarter, the shops are fine

facts.data: orders with date, channel, region, category, amount and status
facts.decision: cut or keep the online ads budget for next quarter

opening: north region, help?

facts.situation: sales in the north region are lower than same time last year, other regions grew
